subject: Archaeology
title: Angkor Wat: Hidden in the Jungle
description: A micro-lesson that makes Angkor Wat: Hidden in the Jungle usable.

hook.text: A French explorer in 1860 stumbled onto the largest religious monument on earth, swallowed by Cambodian jungle.

buildup.text: Angkor Wat was built in the 12th century for the Khmer Empire. Its moat alone is three miles around.

discovery.text: LiDAR scans in 2012 revealed that Angkor was a sprawling metropolis of over a million people.

twist.text: The city collapsed partly because its massive water system could not survive prolonged drought.

climax.text: Angkor Wat never truly vanished — Buddhist monks maintained the central temple for centuries.

punchline.text: The 'lost' temple was never lost. Monks kept it alive while the city fell.

quiz.question: What did LiDAR scans reveal about Angkor in 2012?
options: The temple was much older than previously believed
Angkor was a sprawling metropolis of over a million people
A network of underground tunnels connected all the temples

details.summary: Angkor Wat in Cambodia, the world's largest religious monument, was built in the early 12th century by King Suryavarman II. Though never completely abandoned, it was overgrown by jungle for centuries until French explorers brought it to Western attention in 1860.
details.whyItMatters: Angkor Wat demonstrates the scale of the Khmer Empire's ambition and engineering. Recent LiDAR surveys show the temple was the center of a metropolitan area larger than modern Paris — quietly disproving the myth of a lost city.
takeaways: The world's largest religious monument, built in the 12th century
LiDAR revealed a vast surrounding city hidden under jungle
It was maintained continuously by Buddhist monks for centuries

faq.question: Was Angkor Wat really lost?
faq.answer: Not to local people. Cambodians always knew about it, and Buddhist monks maintained the temple continuously. It was lost only to Western knowledge until Henri Mouhot's visit in 1860. The narrative of European discovery erases centuries of local stewardship and knowledge.

faq.question: What did LiDAR reveal about Angkor?
faq.answer: Airborne LiDAR stripped away jungle canopy to reveal an enormous urban landscape with roads, canals, reservoirs, and residential areas extending far beyond the temple complex. Greater Angkor covered over 1,000 square kilometers — one of the largest pre-industrial cities in history.
